sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the civic and commercial centre of Salem at 50 feet to an inch. It is drawn turned about thirty degrees to the street grid, so Market Street runs down the left centre of the page and West and East Broadway cross it as a gently curving line at the lower third. The upper left shows the west side of Market Street, a row of long residential lots with frame dwellings, a church and the Salem County Memorial Hospital and Historical Society, running back toward Griffith Street. The upper right is the open block of the county seat: the Salem County Court House, County Offices, County Office Building, the jail with a 100 foot stand pipe, the Liberty and Union fire company houses, the First Presbyterian Church and the Salem Graded School, with Grant Street along the top edge and a Friends Meeting House and Sunday School toward the right. Along the south side of East Broadway and both sides of West Broadway the drawing becomes dense brick business frontage: the City National Bank and Trust Company, Green's Hotel, the Palace and Fenwick theatres, the New Johnson Hotel, the Post Office, the Salem National Bank and Trust Company, the Nelson House, the Sunbeam Publishing Company and the Mecum Building, with the City of Salem Municipal Building behind. The bottom of the sheet shows New Market Street, Walnut Street and Hedge Street with garages, auto repair and service stations, dress manufacturing and the Armory of the Company T.N.G. of N.J. Water pipes are lettered along the streets and numbers of adjoining sheets 3, 4, 5, 6, 13 and 14 are printed at the edges.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 30 degrees from north; the printed north arrow is not reliable for this.
Hedge Street at the bottom left is today's Hires Avenue only near Chestnut Street (the modern Hires Avenue was cut through at another angle); the rest of the old street is gone.
Modern Walnut Street and New Market Street are displaced from their drawn lines by several metres to tens of metres and were left out of the control.
Control is sparse (Broadway junctions only); distances between modern junctions are about 10 percent longer than on the sheet east to west, so the fit is low confidence.

Salem business centre: Market, Griffith, Grant, West and East Broadway, New Market, Walnut, Chestnut, Hedge; court house, county offices, jail. 50 ft. One part. Few surviving junctions (Walnut and New Market displaced); fitted scale about 11 percent under the atlas (low confidence).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the east side of Salem at 50 feet to an inch, drawn turned about thirty degrees to the street grid so that Grant Street runs across the top and East Broadway crosses the lower part of the page from upper left to lower right. The upper half is a district of single-family frame dwellings, mostly two and a half storeys, set on deep narrow lots with house numbers lettered along the street: the west side of 7th Street, the blocks between 7th and 8th Streets facing Grant Street, and the long lots on the south side of Grant east of 8th Street. The centre of the sheet is a large undeveloped block with the compass rose, and the numbers of neighbouring sheets 2, 4, 14, 15 and 16 are printed at the edges. East Broadway at the bottom is drawn as a wide street with a continuous row of small frame dwellings and shops along its north side, among them the Memorial Baptist Church at the west end, a plumber, an auto painting shop and the Club F.O.E., with a diagonal lane behind. To the right, Craven Avenue crosses the sheet down to 9th Street, serving a few scattered houses and a small brick building, with open lots to the north. Eakin Street leaves East Broadway at the bottom edge. Water pipes with their diameters are marked along 7th, 8th and 9th Streets, Grant Street and East Broadway. At the left edge a strip of commercial buildings and two larger pink brick buildings belong to the next sheet, number 2.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 30 degrees from north.
East Broadway is drawn very wide; the modern centreline lies along the north building line, so the Eakin Street / East Broadway junction could not be detected and is not in the control.
Salem east of centre: Grant, 7th, 8th, 9th Streets, Craven Avenue, East Broadway, Eakin Street. 50 ft. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the railroad corridor and the northern edge of Salem's built-up area at 50 feet to an inch, drawn turned about thirty degrees to the street grid; Market Street runs diagonally down the left edge and Grant Street along the bottom. The middle of the page is taken up by the broad bundle of tracks of the W.J.&S.R.R. running from the top to the lower right, with a curving spur toward the Green Bros. works and a railroad water tank at the top. Along the left side the long lots between Market Street and the tracks hold frame dwellings and, at the north, Rex Alley with a row of dwellings and Colored Tenements; Green Bros. appear as a block of farm implement warehouses, coal silos and a mill building with a concrete block works and a lime tank. St. John's Episcopal Church with its Sunday School and a cemetery lie below them, and the Wistar and Woodnutt lumber yard with sheds, a garage, a hardware and paint shop and an oil store fills the bottom left corner at Grant and Griffith Streets. East of the tracks are the Salem City Milling Company grist mill and its feed storage, a freight house and the Passenger Station, then the blocks between Hubbell Avenue and 7th Street with the extensive Ayars Machine Company works and rows of frame dwellings along Pledger, Gibbon and Grant Streets. Block numbers and neighbouring sheets 2, 3, 5, 9, 16 and 19 are lettered on the margins, and 4 inch water pipes are marked in nearly every street.
notes: Hubbell Avenue is today's Hubble Avenue.
The alley name near the top left is lettered partly with numerals and was read as Rex Alley; the reading is uncertain.
Drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 30 degrees from north.
The Salem Branch tracks drawn through the middle of the sheet lie about 7 m from the modern line (measured at six points).
Salem: West Jersey and Seashore Railroad corridor and the Hubbell Avenue blocks between Market and 7th Streets, Pledger, Gibbon, Grant. 50 ft. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the north-west part of Salem at 50 feet to an inch and is drawn nearly square to the page, with north up. Fenwick Creek curves down the upper left corner. Below it, along the creek and Hancock Street, stand the industrial works of the district: the Salem Coal, Ice and Storage Company with its cold storage, ice storage, engine room and coal sheds, and the Atlantic City Electric Company sub-station, drawn in pink brick. In the centre the Salem Gas Light Company occupies a large lot with a coal house, purifying room, engine house and two round gas holders, and the W.J.&S.R.R. siding and main line sweep across the sheet from the lower left to the upper right. The rest of the page is residential: narrow lots with frame dwellings, mostly two storeys with outbuildings, in the blocks along 5th Street, between 5th Street and Ward Street, and between Ward Street and Market Street, with house numbers lettered along the fronts. Howell Street crosses the upper blocks, where a livery and a storage building and a junk yard lie at the north-east, and Griffith Street closes the bottom of the sheet, where a machine shop and Biberman Bros. occupy the corner by Ward Street. The upper margin is marked vacant beyond. Water pipes with their diameters are lettered in most streets, and the numbers of neighbouring sheets 1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 17, 18, 20 and 134 are printed on the page.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch; the compass rose is aligned with the page, but the street grid is turned about 6 degrees from north.
The Hancock Street / Market Street junction lies just beyond the right edge of the scan and is placed from the drawn street edge.
The Market / Grant / Griffith junction at the bottom right lies on the margin and was not detected.
Salem north-west: Fenwick Creek works, gas works, 5th, Ward, Market, Howell, Hancock Streets. 50 ft. One part.

sheet-6-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 6 is the main map, at 50 feet to an inch, covering the blocks of central Salem between Griffith Street at the top and West Broadway at the bottom, with 5th Street running down the middle and Ward Street meeting Griffith at the right. The upper right quarter of the sheet is taken by an inset of a different place and is not part of this area. West of 5th Street the sheet is mostly open ground: the Salem Sash Factory with its planing mill and cabinet shop on Griffith, a welding shop and laundry, the storage yard of the Salem Glass Works with piles of wooden crates, and the large Friend's Cemetery, which fills the lower left quarter. A siding of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (W.J.&S.R.R.) curves down the left side past the sash factory. Along 5th Street and the south side of Griffith stand rows of frame dwellings and some apartments, and towards West Broadway the block holds St. John's Episcopal Parish House and the John Tyler Library. East of 5th Street are dwellings, sheds, a mission and plumbers' storage, and on West Broadway the Y.M.C.A. and the 1st Baptist Church. Water pipes are marked along Griffith, 5th Street and Broadway. The street pattern is sparse: only three junctions of surviving streets are drawn, and Ward Street appears only as a short lane with a water pipe.
notes: Placed from three junctions (Griffith / 5th, Griffith / Ward, 5th / West Broadway), two of them hand-picked: an exact fit with no check; low confidence.
The upper right quarter of the sheet is an inset of the Mannington Mills Inc. felt base floor covering plant, configured separately or left unplaced.

Salem: Griffith, 5th St, Ward St, West Broadway; Friend's Cemetery, Salem Sash Factory. 50 ft. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset (upper right, own north arrow) of Mannington Mills Inc. felt base floor covering plant beyond Claysville, no street junction (unplaced).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Mannington Mills Inc. felt base floor covering plant (no street junction; plant largely rebuilt; needs parcel corners or rail control along the Salem Branch).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the west side of Salem at 50 feet to an inch, drawn turned about fourteen degrees to the street grid. Griffith Street crosses the upper part of the page from left to right, 4th Street runs down the centre, 3rd Street runs down the left edge and West Broadway closes the bottom. The upper centre and right are filled by the Salem Glass Works: the 3rd Street Plant at the top, with its furnace, lehrs, storage of paper cartons and a large yellow warehouse on the left (the plant has a note to see the report on Sheet 10), and the 4th Street Plant between 4th Street and the railroad, with furnace, grinding and pug mill rooms, batch house, sand storage and long ware sheds and storage buildings. Further storage sheds marked 77 to 82 lie along the railroad and siding at the top right, and a railroad line curves through the right side. Between 3rd and 4th Streets and along Griffith Street the sheet shows blocks of small frame dwellings on narrow lots, house numbers lettered along the fronts, the Griffith Street Public School, 3rd Street Alley, a candy store and a machine shop and mould rooms of the glass company. The lower third is largely open: a few scattered dwellings and a kindergarten front West Broadway, and Friends Cemetery occupies the lower right. Water pipes with diameters are lettered along 3rd Street, 4th Street, Griffith Street and West Broadway, and neighbouring sheets 6, 8, 10 and 12 are numbered on the margins.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 14 degrees from north.

Only three junctions could be used as control (4th Street / West Broadway and 3rd Street / West Broadway detected, 4th Street / Griffith Street hand-picked at the meeting of the water pipes); the fit is exact through three points and is low confidence.
The Salem Glass Works 3rd Street Plant at the top left continues on Sheet 10.
Salem west: Salem Glass Works 3rd Street plant, Griffith, 3rd and 4th Streets, West Broadway. 50 ft. One part; three-point exact fit (low confidence).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers a block-and-a-half wide district on the west side of Salem at 50 feet to an inch, between Front Street on the west and 3rd Street on the east, and from Griffith Street along the top to West Broadway along the bottom. Griffith Street crosses the sheet at a slant, and the blocks beneath it are lined with rows of small frame dwellings on narrow lots, many of them semi-detached or in terraces. In the upper left corner a railroad siding of the West Jersey and Seashore line cuts diagonally across Front Street past a bottling works, a blacksmith shop and a filling shed. The block between Front Street and Hall's Avenue holds storage buildings for the Gayner Glass Works, including a large building labelled Miscellaneous Storage, and further south the Gayner Glass Works Nos. 18 and 17 stand near the foot of the block along with their own storage. Hall's Avenue and 2nd Street run north and south through the middle of the sheet between rows of dwellings; Bethany Mission, a Sunday school and meeting hall, stands on Hall's Avenue near Griffith Street. East of 2nd Street the blocks toward 3rd Street contain more dwellings, a boat shop, a slaughter house, an auto truck garage and a small stable group. The bottom of the sheet is West Broadway, with its water pipe, and the lots on the north side are numbered 44 to 80. Water pipes with their diameters, hydrants, block numbers and lot numbers are printed throughout. The margins carry the numbers of adjoining sheets 7, 9, 10 and 12, the sheet number 8 and the scale bar.
notes: Hall's Avenue and 2nd Street no longer exist as streets in the modern street network.

The drawn Front Street / Griffith Street corner lies about 45 m east-southeast of the modern Front / Griffith / South Broadway node, because Front Street and South Broadway have been realigned; it is not used as control.

Control is the line of West Broadway: the Front Street junction and the water-pipe junctions of Halls Avenue, 2nd Street and 3rd Street, carried from sheet 12 (a similarity fit from collinear points; low confidence for position across the sheet).

Salem west: Front, Griffith, Hall's Av, 2nd St, 3rd St, West Broadway. 50 ft. One part. Hall's Av and 2nd St no longer exist; placed from West Broadway points carried from sheet 12 (helmert along one street). The drawn Front / Griffith corner is about 45 m from both modern Front / Griffith nodes.

sheet-9-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 9 is the main map, at 50 feet to an inch, covering the west end of Salem between Salem Creek and Front Street, from Griffith Street at the top right to West Broadway at the bottom. Salem Creek winds through the left half of the part and the open marsh and yard land along it. The largest works is the Gayner Glass Works, which fills the lower right with its furnaces, lehrs, ovens, sand house, box factory, shipping shed and storage buildings, with its own fire protection notes. Above it along Front Street stand Abbott's Alderney Dairies with a powdered milk plant, freezing tanks and cold storage, the F. H. Lloyd Co. flour mill (not running), the William H. Harris Jr. boat shop on the creek, and the North Bend Hose Company fire house. Two lines of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad cross the part diagonally from the lower left towards Griffith Street, with sidings into the glass works, and a yard full of packing hay and wood bottles lies beside them. A concrete bridge carries the road to Pennsville over the creek at the top right. A row of small dwellings lines the north side of West Broadway at the bottom. The upper left of the sheet, behind a heavy line, is a separate part.
notes: The drawn junction of Front and Griffith is the modern node where South Broadway (the road to Pennsville) leaves Front Street; the modern Griffith Street node 45 m to the south is a later alignment and was excluded.
Placed from two hand-picked junctions (helmert); low confidence.

Salem west end: Front St, Salem Creek, Gayner Glass Works, Abbott's Alderney Dairies (part 1); upper left behind a heavy line with own north arrow: Market St at Fenwick Creek and Hancock St (part 2). 50 ft. Two parts.

sheet-9-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 9 is the upper left area behind a heavy line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow. It shows Market Street north of the business district, from Hancock Street up across Fenwick Creek, where Market Street crosses on a concrete bridge, to the blocks on the north bank. Fenwick Creek runs across the upper half of the part with Salem Creek below. South of the creek are the Farmers Exchange warehouse and the C. G. Lippincott coal yard with open corn bins and storage, the Standard Oil Company and The Texas Co. oil station with their tanks at the left edge, and grain and other storage buildings. A siding of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad crosses the part from the left towards Market Street. North of the creek, at the top, stand a garage and a farm implements store on Market Street. The lower part shows the frame dwellings along Market Street between the siding and Hancock Street, the small Rex Alley (arbitrary) off the east side of Market, and junk storage buildings west of Market. Hancock Street leaves Market at the lower left and runs west to the edge of the part.
notes: Anchored on one detected junction (Market / Hancock) with the atlas scale; rotation from the drawn street lines: low confidence.
Rex Alley is marked arbitrary on the sheet.

Salem west end: Front St, Salem Creek, Gayner Glass Works, Abbott's Alderney Dairies (part 1); upper left behind a heavy line with own north arrow: Market St at Fenwick Creek and Hancock St (part 2). 50 ft. Two parts.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows the industrial strip along the north side of Salem at 50 feet to an inch, between Salem Creek and Fenwick Creek. The sheet is turned so that Griffith Street runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, and the plan is drawn at an angle of about thirty degrees to the usual orientation, with its own north arrow in the lower left. Most of the sheet is given to two large works. H. J. Heinz Co., Branch No. 12, Canning and Bottling Works, occupies the upper middle: a very large can house and storage building with a brick floor, the bottling and warehouse blocks, receiving and basket storage sheds, a kitchen and a cyclone, a vinegar house, a covered reservoir of 15,000 gallons, a power house and an underwriters fire pump, with a long table of watchman, power, lighting, water supply and fire protection particulars printed at the lower left. Railroad tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore line and sidings swing across the sheet and into the works. The Salem Glass Works plant fills the lower right, with long storage warehouses, a large steel frame building with wood sheathing under an iron roof containing a row of lehrs, three round tanks, a batch house, a time office and fuel oil tanks. At the left a few frame dwellings face Griffith Street between Hall's Avenue and 2nd Street, and a concrete bridge carries Front Street toward the top left corner. Water pipes, hydrants and fire hose are marked throughout. The lower left is blank because it belongs to sheet 8, and sheet 7 adjoins at the lower right.
notes: Control is a single point, the Front Street / Griffith Street water-pipe corner carried from sheet 8, with scale and rotation taken from sheet 8 and from the direction of the Griffith Street water pipe; low confidence. The modern line of Griffith Street lies along the drawn street.
Hall's Avenue and 2nd Street no longer exist as streets in the modern street network; Third Street is drawn as a street inside the Salem Glass Works plant and has no modern node.
The drawn Front Street / Griffith Street corner is about 45 m from the modern Front / Griffith / South Broadway node, which is not used.

Salem: H. J. Heinz Co. Branch No. 12 canning works and Salem Glass Works plant between Front St, Griffith, 2nd and 3rd Streets, Salem Creek and Fenwick Creek. 50 ft. One part, anchored on the Front / Griffith corner carried from sheet 8 (low confidence).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the southwest edge of Salem at 50 feet to an inch: marsh and creek bank west of Tilbury Avenue and south of West Broadway. West Broadway runs across the top of the sheet, with Front Street meeting it at the upper right corner, and the blocks above it belong to sheet 9. The main feature is Plant No. 1 of the Congoleum Nairn Co. Inc., linoleum makers, drawn as a cluster of sprinklered brick and concrete buildings between Tilbury Avenue and a curving railroad siding: the print rooms, the drying houses Nos. 1 and 8, the hand printing and linoleum drying rooms Nos. 15 and 16, a machine shop, a packing building, storage buildings Nos. 14, 29 and 30, a transformer house and a water tank on a steel trestle, with a table of watchman, steam power and fire protection details beside the name. A railroad siding of the West Jersey and Seashore line enters from the top and curves southward through the plant, and a second line runs along the west side. West of the siding the Gayner Glass Works keeps a fenced yard for glass jars piled eight feet high and a few outbuildings; a fertilizer storage building, a small group of dwellings, a boat shop and a sewage pumping station stand on the marshy ground near Salem Creek, which curves down the left side. A drainage channel crosses the bottom of the sheet and the land south of it is marsh. Most of the sheet is open land with no streets.
notes: Only one modern street junction survives on this sheet (Front Street / West Broadway, at the upper right corner), so the part is anchored on it with the sheet scale and a rotation measured from the line of West Broadway; low confidence.
Tilbury Avenue, as drawn along the east side of the plant, no longer exists as a street in the modern network.
The sheet number 144 near the bottom is a block number, and the neighbouring sheets 5, 9 and 12 are named in the margins.
Salem south-west: West Broadway at Tilbury Av, Congoleum Nairn Co. plant no. 1, Salem Creek, Drainage Channel. 50 ft. One part, anchored on Front / West Broadway (low confidence).

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows the southwest part of Salem at 100 feet to an inch, along the south side of West Broadway from Front Street to beyond 4th Street, and southward to a drainage channel. West Broadway runs across the top, with its water pipes, and the cross streets Front Street, Halls Avenue, 2nd Street, 3rd Street and 4th Street are drawn only for a short stretch above it, where they belong to sheets 9, 8 and 7. The strip of lots numbered 45 to 109 along the south side of Broadway is lined with frame dwellings, a gasoline station and, at the left, the office of the Congoleum Co. Inc. Below it lies a grid of narrow lots between Hedge, Carpenter and Thompson streets, crossed by 3rd Street and Miller Street, packed with small frame dwellings, many in uniform rows; block numbers 26 to 31 and 319 and 320 are printed here. Friends Meeting House stands near the right edge on Broadway. At the left the Congoleum Co. Inc. Plant No. 2 occupies a long brick building with print and drying rooms, oil houses and oil tanks beside Tilbury Avenue, which runs down the left edge. South of the built-up blocks the sheet is open meadow, crossed from upper left to lower right by the Drainage Channel, and Oak Street Road leaves the lower right corner. Streets west of 3rd Street along Hedge and Carpenter are drawn without buildings. The adjoining sheets 4, 8, 7, 9, 11 and 13 are named in the margins.
notes: Halls Avenue and 2nd Street, and Tilbury Avenue, no longer exist as streets in the modern street network; Front Street south of West Broadway is now South Front Street.
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with a scale bar at the foot of the sheet.

The detector's measure of the 3rd Street / West Broadway junction was rejected (11 m from the fit, from a narrow edge pair); the eight junctions used lie along Broadway and the Hedge, Carpenter and Thompson rows.
Salem south-west: West Broadway, Halls Av, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Streets, Hedge, Carpenter, Thompson, Miller, Oak Street Road, Tilbury Av; Drainage Channel. 100 ft. One part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the south side of Salem at 100 feet to an inch, from West Broadway at the top to Smith Street and the Drainage Channel at the bottom, and from Oak Street at the left to Walnut Street at the right. The area is a built-up grid of frame dwellings on narrow lots. At the top, Broadway M.E. Church and the American Legion building stand on the south side of West Broadway, and the numbered blocks below hold rows of dwellings along Hedge, Carpenter, Thompson and Wesley streets. Alvin W. Davis lumber yard with its sheds and a garage lie east of Chestnut Street. The center of the sheet is held by Salem High School, near Wesley Street, and Richard M. Acton Public School stands to the east between Belden Street and Church Street, with the First M.E. Church south of it. St. Mary's R.C. Church and its parish house are at the left between Carpenter and Thompson. Chestnut Street, Van Meter Terrace and New Market Street run south toward Smith Street, and Maple Avenue and two lanes run diagonally across the southern end of the sheet, where the blocks thin out into open ground. A bridge carries a road over the Drainage Channel at the lower left, and Oak Street Road runs down the left margin. A small group of dwellings stands on Walnut Street Lane in the lower right. Sheets 12, 6, 2 and 14 adjoin and are named in the margins; block numbers run from 147 to 332.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
Printed street names such as Chestnut and Wesley carry no suffix on the sheet; modern names are Chestnut Street and Wesley Street, and Van Meter Terrace is printed Van Meter Ter.
The fit is second order (20 points, RMSE about 2.3 m, leave-one-out about 3.5 m); Maple Avenue / Van Meter Terrace and Oak Street / Wesley Street carry residuals of about 6 m.
Salem south: West Broadway, Hedge, Carpenter, Thompson, Wesley, Oak, Chestnut, Van Meter Terrace, New Market, Walnut, Church, Sinnickson, Smith, Maple Av. 100 ft. One part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the east side of Salem at 100 feet to an inch, a large residential district south and east of the business centre. It runs from Walnut Street on the west across Eakin Street, the angled course of East Broadway and the parallel streets Olive, Union, Elm and Linden to North Elm and North Union at the east, and from Craven and Morrison Avenues at the top to the vacant land south of Magnolia Street at the bottom. The west part is a regular grid of narrow lots between Church Street, Wesley, Sinnickson and Smith, lined with rows of small frame dwellings, many of them semi-detached; east of Eakin the streets turn to follow East Broadway, which crosses the sheet diagonally with larger houses, a filling station and stores at its west end near the business district. The Second Baptist Church (colored) stands on Eakin Street, and a few brick and stone buildings are scattered among the frame houses. The upper right corner shows the blocks along Craven Avenue, 1st Avenue and Morrison Avenue between 9th Street, Johnson and North Union. Water pipes are marked along most streets with their diameters, and fire hydrants and telephone poles are shown. The lower half south of Smith Street and Magnolia is lightly built, with long lots along Olive, Union, Elm and Linden, and the bottom margin is marked vacant beyond. Block numbers and the numbers of adjoining sheets 2, 3, 13, 15 and 16 are printed along the edges.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
1st Avenue (between Johnson and North Union) is today's Allen Avenue.
East Broadway junctions were not detected; the fit rests on the side streets (residuals up to about 9 m, a sheet drawn with some internal inconsistency).
Salem east side: Walnut, Eakin, Church, Wesley, Sinnickson, Smith, East Broadway, Olive, Union, Elm, Linden, Magnolia, Craven, Morrison. 100 ft. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the southeast edge of Salem at 100 feet to an inch, where East Broadway divides into three roads. East Broadway enters from the upper left and runs southeast to a fork in the middle of the sheet; from there York Street runs southwest, Keasbey Street northeast and Quinton Street east-southeast. Linden Street crosses from the left to meet Broadway, and N. Elm and Elm St. join it near the top. The built-up frontage is thickest along East Broadway and around the fork, with frame dwellings, stores, auto sales and filling stations, a gasoline filling station, and on Broadway the Colored Odd Fellows Hall and the Washington Fire Department. Mt. Hope M.E. Church (colored) stands on the upper part of Broadway, and an A.M.E. church sits on York Street. Long narrow lots with rows of dwellings line Keasbey Street to the upper right edge and Roe Avenue, where Auto Sales and Service buildings stand. Quinton Street runs out to East View Cemetery at the right edge, and the Baptist Cemetery lies along York Street at the lower left. Magnolia Street crosses the left of the sheet and Kent Street is drawn at the foot, below block 204. Much of the lower right is open farm land, marked as such. Block numbers 105, 108 to 112 and 151 are printed.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
York is Yorke Street today, and Quinton Street east of the fork is the continuation of East Broadway (modern East Broadway runs to Quinton Road).
Fitted scale is about 3.85 px per foot, 4 to 5 percent below the other 100 ft sheets; the overlay with modern streets and parcels agrees across the sheet.
Salem south-east: East Broadway (Quinton road), North Elm, Elm, Linden, Magnolia, York, Keasbey, Roe Av, Kent; East View and Baptist cemeteries. 100 ft. One part.

sheet-16-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 16 is the main map, at 100 feet to an inch, covering the north-east edge of Salem between Fenwick Creek and Grant Street. It shows the residential blocks along 7th Street and 8th Street crossed by Pledger, Pearl, Gibbon and Grant, with Hubbell Avenue at the upper left, and the open ground east of 8th Street running out to the marsh along the creek. Small frame dwellings fill most lots, with a few stores, sheds and a milk depot near Grant Street. At the upper left the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad lines run north to a bridge over Fenwick Creek, beside the Salem Supply Co. canning factory and the Horner Foundry Co. casting room. The lower right corner reaches south of Grant Street to 9th Street, Craven Avenue and Morrison Avenue, with a contractor's storage building. The lower left quarter of the sheet, behind a heavy line, is an inset of Claysville and is a separate part. Water pipes are marked along the streets with their diameters, and block numbers and the numbers of adjoining sheets 3, 4 and 14 are printed.
notes: Hubbell Avenue is spelled Hubble Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.

Salem north-east: Hubbell Av, 7th, 8th, Pledger, Pearl, Gibbon, Grant (part 1); lower left behind a heavy line: inset of Claysville (Market St = Salem-Woodstown Road, Booker Alley, Washington Al., Tee Alley, West Av, Bank St, Factory) (part 2). 100 ft. Two parts.

sheet-16-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 16 is an inset of Claysville, the village immediately north of Salem along the road to Woodstown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch in the lower left quarter of the sheet behind a heavy line. Market Street runs down the middle of the inset. East of it, Booker Alley and Washington Alley run to Tee Alley, enclosing a block with the New Jerusalem A.U.M.P. Church (colored); shacks (colored) stand at the top of Market Street. West of Market Street are the public school and scattered dwellings, and further south Market Street Lane, West Avenue and Bank Street branch off to the south-west, lined with small frame houses and a bakery. Factory, marked arbitrary, leaves Market Street towards the south-east, past the Sinclair Refining Co. pumping station and the Salem Glass Co. storage buildings beside a curving line of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad. Much of the inset is marked vacant beyond. Block numbers are printed, and the inset has its own north arrow.
notes: Market Street in Claysville is today's Salem-Woodstown Road; Booker Alley, Tee Alley and Washington Alley are today's Booker Street loop and Church Street; Factory follows today's Mannington Mills Road.
Placed from three hand-picked junctions (an exact fit); the overlay of modern parcels and roads matched the drawn lots and Market Street; medium to low confidence.

Salem north-east: Hubbell Av, 7th, 8th, Pledger, Pearl, Gibbon, Grant (part 1); lower left behind a heavy line: inset of Claysville (Market St = Salem-Woodstown Road, Booker Alley, Washington Al., Tee Alley, West Av, Bank St, Factory) (part 2). 100 ft. Two parts.

sheet-17-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 17 is the main map of Quinton, a village on the road three miles east of Salem Court House, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about twenty-five degrees from north so that Main Street runs up the page. Alloway Creek crosses the top of the part from left to right, with a bridge carrying the Road to Salem over it. Isaac S. Swick and Son's lumber, feed and coal yard stands beside the creek, and the Fogg and Hires Co. canning factory, with its process rooms and warehouses, lies at the upper right beside the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad. Main Street is the spine of the village, lined with small frame dwellings, shops, a garage, the Quinton Fire Co., a public school, the M. E. Church and a Baptist church. Cottage Avenue, Beasley, East Avenue and Lake cross it, with Smithfield parallel to it on the west and High on the east, and Robinson closes the part at the foot where Main Street bends south-east. A second Fogg and Hires Co. canning factory stands east of Main Street, with rows of small dwellings along the road lettered Alloway at the upper right. Large unbuilt tracts and marsh fill the middle east. Two further parts of the sheet, the Waterworks area at the lower right and a strip of Main Street at the lower left, are drawn behind heavy lines.
notes: Main is today's Cross Road and Robinson is Robinson Road; no other street of this part survives as a modern named junction, so the part rests on that single junction.

Placed as an anchored part: one junction (Cross Road / Robinson Road) with the scale from the other village sheets (3.99 px/ft) and a rotation of about 23 degrees taken from the measured lines; low confidence.
The red OpenStreetMap line of Cross Road bends away from the drawn Main Street towards the north (up to about 40 m at Cottage Avenue), so the placement is best near the Robinson junction.

Quinton (village east of Salem). 100 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Main St = Cross Road, Robinson Road), anchored on one junction; 2 lower right (waterworks, Kelty canning factory, filter plant, Laurel Lake) and 3 lower left (Main Street south of Robinson) unplaced.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: lower right: waterworks, Kelty canning factory, filter plant, Laurel Lake (no street junction; needs carried or parcel-corner points (step 6b)).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: lower left: strip of Main Street south of Robinson (no cross street; needs parcel corners along Main Street (step 6b)).

sheet-18-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 18 is the main map of Alloway, a village about six miles east of Salem Court House, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about twenty degrees on the page. Main Street runs diagonally across the sheet from upper left to lower right and crosses the north-south street lettered Main or Greenwich at the middle of the village, where Hotel Alloway, the post office, the Alloway Township Fire Co. and a cluster of shops stand. Canal Street runs parallel to Main Street a block to the north, with Water, Cedar, Penn and Church Streets crossing the blocks, and Lambert Street runs east and west south of Main Street. Most of the village is small frame dwellings on narrow lots with numbered lot lines. Industrial features lie in the north: the Ewen Milling Co. (steam-powered mill with a feed warehouse), lumber sheds, and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, which curves across the top of the sheet beside Alloway Creek, with a head race running east from the creek. Other named works are the Shiveler Milk Co. dairy and feed stores, the J. W. Dunham abattoir and the Alloway Township School, with its auditorium, at the foot of the sheet where the Road to Friesburg leaves Greenwich Street. The south and east are mostly vacant land marked no exposure. A text panel gives the population (1,400), the absence of water facilities and the Alloway Township and East Ward fire companies. The inset in the upper right corner is part 2.
notes: Main (east-west) is today's West Main Street and East Main Street; Greenwich is South Greenwich Street and North Greenwich Street; Canal is East Canal Street; Penn is today's Birch Street; Church, Cedar and Lambert are Church Street, Cedar Street and Lambert Street; the Road to Friesburg is Alloway Friesburg Road.

The N-S street Water at the left corresponds to today's String Street (continuing north as Water Street). The east-west Water Street and West Canal Street of the modern map were not used: West Canal Street is about 35 m out of line with the drawn Canal.
Placed from 10 detected junctions (RMSE about 2.7 m, leave-one-out about 4.3 m); the Birch / East Canal point is about 5 m off the fit.
Alloway (village). 100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset at upper right behind a heavy line (Canal and Church, Ewen's Lake), anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-18-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 18 is an inset in the upper right corner of the sheet, behind a heavy line, showing the east end of Alloway at 100 feet to an inch. Canal Street runs from the left edge towards the lower right, lined with numbered lots (176 to 188) and small dwellings, with a foundation for the East Ward Fire Co. near its beginning. Church Street runs down the left side of the inset beside the heavy boundary line, with the M. E. Church, a pink-coloured brick or stone building, standing in the field to its east. The Cemetery is lettered across the lower part of the inset, above the heavy line that closes it at the bottom and a north arrow and compass rose that overlap the boundary. Ewen's Lake appears along the top and on the left of the inset. Further dwellings and a farm group stand in the upper right. Block numbers 305 and 307 are printed, and the sheet number 18 and the Salem oval with the January 1930 date fill the right side.
notes: Canal and Church are today's East Canal Street and Church Street in Alloway.

Placed from a single hand-picked junction (Church Street / East Canal Street) with the scale and rotation of the main part: an anchored fit, low confidence. The overlay of modern roads agreed with the drawn Canal Street.
Alloway (village). 100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset at upper right behind a heavy line (Canal and Church, Ewen's Lake), anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 maps the Delaware River front of Pennsville, six miles west of Salem Court House, at 100 feet to an inch and turned about forty degrees from north so that the river runs down the left side of the page. The sheet is dominated by amusement-park and waterfront development in the upper half: boardwalks lined with concession buildings, a cone pool, a carrousel, a dance hall, a roller coaster, the Whip, Scooter, a Tumble Bug and a little wild cat ride laid out among winding paths, with a driveway leading east towards the Pennsgrove road. Along the river front a long pier, marked pile substructure, runs out from the end of Pittfield Street, with a hotel, the Riverview Hotel, a second carrousel, a dance hall and a bar and hotel at the south end of the built-up area. Pittfield Street and Main Street run east across the sheet through small frame dwellings on narrow numbered lots, with Front Street joining them near the river and a cemetery at the east edge. A fire company building and town hall stand near Pennsgrove at the right edge. Two ferry slips with pile substructures and a line of small waterfront buildings occupy the lower left. Picnic Grove and a small lake are lettered in the open ground. The sheet refers the reader to sheet 20 for the report on the town and carries a north arrow, turned well off vertical, in the upper left.
notes: Pittfield is today's West Pittsfield Street and East Pittsfield Street; Pennsgrove is North Broadway; Trinity Street or Salem Road is South Broadway; Hook Road is the continuation of East Pittsfield Street. Front Street and Main Street keep their names.

The drawn Front Street jogs where it crosses Pittfield Street (the part north of it is shifted about 180 px, roughly 45 ft, from the part south), which the modern line does not show; the Front Street junctions are therefore weaker control.
Placed from four junctions (two detected, two hand-picked) with a first-order fit of about 5 m RMSE; scale 4.0 px/ft agrees with the other sheets. Low confidence.
Pennsville river front: Pittfield, Front, Main, Pennsgrove, Hook Road; Delaware River. 100 ft. One part, weak (4 points, 2 hand-picked).

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 continues Pennsville to the east and south-east of sheet 19, at 100 feet to an inch and turned about forty degrees from north. Pennsgrove, a street of detached dwellings on regular lots, runs down the left side of the sheet from the top to a bend near the middle, where it becomes Trinity Street or Salem Road and runs south-east across the lower half of the sheet. Pittfield Street enters from the left and meets Pennsgrove; Hook Road continues east from the same junction in a long line of frame dwellings on narrow lots that crosses the upper part of the sheet. Green Lane, German and an unnamed lane lead off Hook Road into small blocks of houses. South of the bend, Trinity Street or Salem Road is lined with dwellings and the Trinity M. E. Church, with Chestnut, Acton Terrace and Spruce Street laid out on long narrow lots parallel to it and across it to the south-west. Pennsville School No. 2, in pink, stands in open ground in the middle of the sheet, and the text panel at the upper right gives the population (650), the water supply drawn from the Delaware River through a suction pipe, and the Lower Penns Neck fire company. A north arrow in the left margin is turned about forty degrees off vertical. Much of the east and south is vacant land.
notes: Pennsgrove is today's North Broadway; Trinity Street or Salem Road is South Broadway; Pittfield Street and Hook Road are West Pittsfield Street and East Pittsfield Street; Green Lane and German correspond to Union Lane and Church Street, but the names were not checked against any source.

Placed from five detected junctions (RMSE about 4 m, leave-one-out about 13 m); the Main Street / South Broadway junction was excluded because its parcel-derived centre lies 11 m from the OpenStreetMap node. Low confidence.
Pennsville (continued): Pennsgrove, Pittfield, Main, Green Lane, German, Trinity Street or Salem Road. 100 ft. One part, weak.

sheet-21-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 21 is the main map of Fort Elfsborg, a riverside summer settlement on the Delaware River about four miles south-west of Salem, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The left column of the sheet runs from Brant Road at the top down the shore to Riverside Park at the bottom. A row of cottages, most with names such as Eagle-View, Normandy and Hill-Crest, faces the river along the shore road, with marsh land behind. Beach Road curves in from the north and runs south to a small grid of streets in the lower half: Riverview Drive, Nelson Avenue and Delaware Avenue, divided into numbered lots with scattered cottages, a boarding house and a hall near the shore. An electric power plant stands on Beach Road, and a ditch drains the marsh at the lower left beside Riverside Park, where more cottages line the shore. The area to the right of the grid is marked vacant beyond. The upper middle of the sheet, inside a heavy outline, is an inset of the Salem County Country Club and is not part of this area; the two columns at the right are separate strips of the shore further along.
notes: Beach Road here is today's Locust Avenue; the east ends of Riverview Drive and Nelson Avenue meet today's Fort Elfsborg-Salem Road.
Placed from one hand-picked and two detected points; the north end around Brant Road is far from control and may be tens of metres off; low confidence.
Brant Road is marked arbitrary on the sheet.

Fort Elfsborg, 4 miles S.W. of Salem: 100 ft. Four parts: 1 main left column (Beach Road = Locust Avenue, Riverview Drive, Nelson Av, Delaware Av, Brant Road); 2 inset Salem County Country Club (Brant Rd); 3 middle strip (Beach Rd, Riverside Golf Course Park); 4 right strip (Beach Rd, Riverside Park). Parts 2-4 unplaced.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Salem County Country Club and Brant Road (no street junction; needs parcel corners; Brant Road may be today's Country Club Road).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: middle strip: Beach Road and Riverside Golf Course Park (the only junction (Beach Road / Road) could not be matched to a modern node; a trial anchored on South Locust Avenue / Fort Elfsborg-Salem Road did not fit the parcels; needs identification of the shore road south of Fort Elfsborg; parcel corners).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: right strip: Beach Road and Riverside Park (no street junction; needs parcel corners along the shore).

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 maps Hancock's Bridge, a village about six miles south of Salem Court House, at 100 feet to an inch. Alloway Creek crosses the top of the sheet from left to right, with an iron bridge carrying the Road to Salem over it near the upper right and a second bend of the creek along the north edge of the village. Front Street runs north-east along the creek bank past the Edmund Shimp Company canning factory, with its warehouses and sheds, and the Fogg and Hires Company canning factory at the Locust Island Road end. Main Street runs down the sheet through the village, lined with small frame dwellings on narrow lots, a hall, the public school and the M. E. Church. New Street and 2nd Street cross it to Maple Avenue, which bounds a block of dwellings and vacant lots on the east, drawn with a fire department building of the Hancock Bridge Fire Co. Locust Island Road runs along the east side of the sheet through open land of numbered blocks. A branch of Fishing Creek winds along the west side of the village, and the Road to Fishing Creek leaves Main Street at the bottom left. The lower part of the sheet is mostly open ground marked no exposure. The sheet carries a text panel with the population (300), the water facilities (no public water works, fire service from the creek) and the fire department, a north arrow turned about twenty degrees from the street grid, and a scale bar at the lower right.
notes: Front, Main, New, Maple Avenue and 2nd Street correspond to today's Front Street, Main Street, New Street, Maple Avenue and 2nd Street in Hancocks Bridge; the road running west from the end of Front Street is today's Poplar Street.
Locust Island Road was left out of the control: its junctions were not found on the sheet at the modern road's position, so it was not used.
Placed from 7 detected junctions with a fit of 0.7 m RMSE; the north arrow is not used (the grid is turned about 19 degrees).
Hancock's Bridge (village on Alloway Creek): Front, Main, New, Maple Avenue, 2nd Street. 100 ft. One part.
